title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Operations and Templates
author: Marcus Chen
content:
Summary:

This playbook describes Redwood Inference's standard on-call and incident response process, key runbooks, postmortem expectations, rotation guidance, game-day planning, and templates for status page and customer communications. It is the canonical operational reference for engineering teams responsible for production services.

Scope:
- Applies to all production services managed by Engineering and SRE (hosted API, control plane, runtime, Dedicated control plane, console).
- Excludes non-production environments (use per-team dev runbooks).

Goals:
- Restore service quickly and safely.
- Maintain clear customer and internal communications.
- Capture root cause and prevention actions in postmortems.
- Keep on-call workload sustainable with clear rotations and tooling.

Incident severity and response windows:
1) Sev 1 (P0) — System-wide outage or severe data-loss risk
   - SLOs affected: >30% error rate or >5x latency for >5 min for core API
   - Response target: acknowledge within 5 minutes, page escalation in 10 minutes
2) Sev 2 (P1) — Major feature degradation affecting large subsets of customers
   - Acknowledge within 15 minutes, begin mitigation within 30 minutes
3) Sev 3 (P2) — Partial degradation, single-customer impact or non-critical functionality
   - Acknowledge within 1 hour, resolve or schedule workaround within 24 hours
4) Sev 4 (P3) — Minor bug, cosmetic issue, or scheduled maintenance
   - Track in backlog, no immediate paging required

Incident lifecycle (high level):
1. Detection & Acknowledgement
   - Alerts from monitoring, synthetic tests, customer reports, or internal dashboards.
   - On-call engineer acknowledges the page in PagerDuty within the response target.
2. Triage
   - Quickly classify severity, affected services, potential blast radius, and ownership.
   - Add initial notes in the incident channel (#inc-<id>) and the incident tracker (confluence incident template).
3. Mitigation
   - Apply known runbook steps. If no known runbook, apply safe fallbacks: scale up, route traffic away, enable degraded mode.
   - Provide status updates every 15 min for Sev1, every 30–60 min for Sev2.
4. Recovery
   - Verify restoration against SLOs and synthetic checks.
   - Monitor for reoccurrence for at least 2× mean-time-to-recover (MTTR).
5. Post-incident
   - Create a postmortem within 48 hours (draft) and publish a final postmortem within 7 business days.
   - Track action items with owners and target completion dates.

Escalation and ownership:
- First responder: primary on-call for owning service (engineering team).
- Secondary escalation: team lead or secondary on-call.
- PagerDuty escalation policy: 3 attempts at 5-minute intervals, then escalate to SEV duty and SRE lead.
- For cross-service incidents, the SRE on-call becomes incident commander (IC) until a service lead is assigned.

Runbooks (how to write and use):
- All runbooks live in the team wiki and must include: purpose, symptoms, pre-checks, safe mitigation steps, rollback steps, post-incident follow-ups, and test commands.
- Keep commands idempotent and mark steps that require careful coordination ("requires coordinator approval").

Example runbook: API 503 — Upstream Overload
Purpose:
- Mitigate 503s caused by upstream model-serving overload or KV cache saturations.
Symptoms:
- Increased 503 rate in logs (>2% of requests), 95th percentile latency > target, model worker queue length > 80%
Pre-checks:
1) Check alert details and synthetic failure points.
2) Confirm CPU/GPU utilization on model-serving nodes.
Mitigation steps (ordered):
1) Scale model pool: `kubectl scale deployment/model-pool -n inference --replicas=<current+2>` (apply only if capacity available)
2) Reduce incoming concurrency: update route config to lower concurrency_limit to 50% via admin API: `curl -X POST https://admin.internal/... -d '{"concurrency_limit":50}'`
3) Enable degraded-mode caching: toggle feature-flag `degraded_kv_cache=true` in the control plane (requires approval for customer-visible changes)
4) If autoscaling unavailable: route traffic to fallback model variant (see routing playbook).
Verification:
- Confirm error rate falls to baseline and 95th percentile latency returns to SLO.
Rollback:
- Revert scale/config changes after stable 30 minutes of normal metrics.
Post-incident actions:
- Increase model-pool autoscaler buffer by 20% if observed frequent saturation.

Runbook table (summary):
| Symptom | Owner | Immediate action | Escalation | Docs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| API 503s | Serving Runtime | Scale pool, reduce concurrency, route to fallback | SRE lead | /runbooks/api-503 |
| Auth failures | Infra | Check IAM keys, rotate if expired, restart auth service | Security on-call | /runbooks/auth-failure |
| Storage latencies | Eng-Platform | Failover to standby, validate snapshot integrity | Storage lead | /runbooks/storage-latency |

Postmortem policy and template:
- Every Sev1/Sev2 incident must produce a postmortem. Sev3 may produce a postmortem at discretion of the IC.
- Postmortem must include: summary, timeline (UTC), impact statement, root cause analysis (RCA), contributing factors, corrective actions (owner + due date), and follow-ups.

Postmortem template (copy/paste):
Title: [Service] — Short description — YYYY-MM-DD
Status: draft / in_review / published
Severity: Sev1/Sev2/Sev3
Impact: number of customers affected, SLOs impacted, downtime duration
Timeline:
- HH:MM UTC — Event detected (source)
- HH:MM UTC — PagerDuty acknowledged (who)
- HH:MM UTC — First mitigation step applied
Root Cause:
Contributing factors:
Resolution and Recovery:
Action items (owner, due date):
- [ ] Owner — Action — Due date
Lessons learned:

On-call rotations and expectations:
- Primary rotation: weekly for engineering on-call. Shift swap allowed with manager approval; update PagerDuty and calendar.
- SRE on-call: 1:2 rotation, two-week shifts.
- Expected duties: monitor alerts, own incidents, update incident channel, run postmortems, and deliver >1 on-call handoff notes.
- Handovers: publish a short status note at the end of shift with outstanding alerts, ongoing mitigations, and calendar conflicts.

Game days and training:
- Schedule quarterly game days per service group. Objectives: validate runbooks, measure mean-time-to-detect (MTTD) and MTTR, exercise cross-team coordination.
- Game day checklist:
  1) Define scenario and blast radius
  2) Notify leadership and schedule observers
  3) Run scenario in staging or limited production (with safety gates)
  4) Execute post-game debrief and update runbooks/action items

Status page and customer comms templates:
Status page entries (short):
- Title: [Service] Partial Degradation — Model-serving latency increased
- Impact: Customers may experience increased latency and intermittent 5xx errors for the inference API.
- Current Status: Identified — We are investigating root cause and applying mitigations.
- Updated: 2026-02-10T14:12:00Z
- Next Update: 2026-02-10T14:30:00Z

Customer email template (initial):
Subject: [Redwood] Service incident affecting inference API — {short summary}
Body:
Hello {Customer Name},
We are investigating an incident affecting the Redwood inference API that may cause increased latency and intermittent errors. Our on-call SREs are working to identify and mitigate the root cause. We will provide updates every 30 minutes.
If you have a critical dependency, please reply to this message or open a support ticket and mark it as critical.
Sincerely,
Redwood Support

Customer update template (follow-up):
Subject: [Redwood] Update on incident — {short summary}
Body:
Hello {Customer Name},
Update: We have identified a contributing factor and applied mitigations that have reduced errors by ~80%. We are monitoring and expect to have full recovery within approximately 45 minutes. Next update: {time}
Actions for customers (if any):
- For uninterrupted operation, consider switching to the fallback model variant described at {internal link} (team assistance available).

Internal incident channel guidance:
- Use channel name `#inc-<YYYYMMDD>-<service>` and prefix messages with `[INC-<id>]`
- Post the Incident Commander, Primary owner, and secondary contact in the first 5 minutes.
- Record all mitigation steps verbatim and include commands run.

Metrics and dashboards to check (starter list):
- API error rate (5xx) — service-level metric
- 95th/99th percentile latencies per route
- Model-worker queue length and GPU utilization
- Autoscaler events and scaling history
- Synthetic checks and customer-facing health endpoints

Training and continuous improvement:
- Every published postmortem is reviewed in the weekly SRE/serving-runtime retro and action items tracked until complete.
- Quarterly on-call surveys to measure load and identify burnout risks.
